ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is an oscillation part composed of a 32768 Hz crystal and components such as capacitors and resistors, connected to the CD4060 chip in the middle. The CD4060 is labeled with a Q14 output terminal, which is output from pin 3 and connected to the clock input terminal C1 of the 74LS74 on the right. The right side of the 74LS74 has the final output terminal Q, and the figure also shows that this flip-flop is connected in a toggle frequency-division form. Reasoning: The problem statement says that the CD4060 forms a 14-stage frequency divider, so the Q14 output frequency of the CD4060 is 32768 Hz / 2^14 = 32768 / 16384 = 2 Hz. Then the 2 Hz signal of Q14 is sent into the 74LS74, and the 74LS74 is used as a divide-by-two flip-flop, so the final Q terminal frequency is 2 Hz / 2 = 1 Hz.
